subject: Copywriting
title: Classified Ads and the Want Ad
description: A quick, practical guide to Classified Ads and the Want Ad.

hook.text: Classified ads charged by the word. Every letter cost money. This forced writers to be ruthlessly concise.

buildup.text: Abbreviations bloomed: 'rm' for room, 'nr' for near, 'gd cond' for good condition. Brevity was survival.

discovery.text: The constraint created a craft. The best classified writers packed maximum meaning into minimum words.

twist.text: Craigslist killed paid classifieds by making them free. Newspapers lost billions in revenue.

climax.text: Twitter's 140-character limit echoed classifieds. Paying per word and paying per character breed the same skill.

punchline.text: Pay per word, write per word. Constraints make better copy.

quiz.question: Why were classified ads so concise?
options: Advertisers were charged by the word
